tagline: An Indian trail, widened for wagons, kept for stagecoaches.
intro: The byway runs about eighteen miles north from the Shelby County side, through a valley of horse farms and historic homes, churches and cemeteries, with much of the land on either side held by the same families for generations. The piece drawn here is about seven miles of it, coming north into Leeds, a town that grew up along the Little Cahaba River and two railroads.

It began as an Indian trail. Andrew Jackson's scouts widened it in 1812 and 1813, looking for roads for supply wagons, and once settlers came into the valley it became the stagecoach road from Ashville to Montevallo. The Leeds Historical Society marked it in 1998.

moments.title: Leeds
moments.text: Incorporated in 1887, Leeds calls itself the City of Valor for three Medal of Honor recipients from World War II and Korea who made their homes here.

moments.title: John Henry's tunnel
moments.text: Local tradition, backed by the folklorist John Garst, holds that John Henry raced the steam drill at a railroad tunnel in Leeds in the 1880s, and that he was a real man.
